header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Li (Redwood SE), Noah Greene (Redwood CSM); Carlos Reyes (BlueMark Head of ML), Aisha Khan (BlueMark Platform), Marta Lopez (BlueMark Security), Tom B. (BlueMark SRE)
summary: POC weekly sync focused on follow-up to reliability incident last week (intermittent 5xx and timeout spikes). Team discussed root causes, retry/backoff tuning, rate limit behavior, and next steps: share traces, increase temporary limits, run load tests, and schedule deep-dive on KV cache and batching. Customer emphasized SOC2/audit concerns for error logs and data retention.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this tight 45 minutes. i know last week's spike caused headaches so want to walk through what we found and next steps.
[00:18] Carlos: yeah thanks. we saw a few windows - roughly 10:10 to 10:25 our time - where requests started returning 5 5 X and a bunch of client-side timeouts. the error rate peaked at about 6%.
[00:32] Jenna: right, we pulled the gateway logs and saw upstream 503s from one pool, plus some request queuing on the host side. initial theory is contention on the dedicated inference nodes when kv-cache misses aligned with long sequences.
[00:49] Aisha: to add, our workload had a lot of long context prompts that caused sequence lengths > 2k tokens, and we had a batch size bump during that window.
[01:05] Tom B. (SRE): there were also a handful of retries from the app that ended up piling up - backpressure effect. our current client retry is immediate then one retry, no exponential backoff.
[01:22] Samir: ok, that explains amplification. jenna - do you have the trace id sample?
[01:30] Jenna: yes i pasted a snippet to the chat (link). the traces show 502/503 returned after 1.2s processing, but another host threw a 504 timeout at 12s. the transcripting system (fireflies note: transcribed as transcripting) had some mislabels; bucket names appear as K V cash in some logs.
[01:50] Marta (Security): quick security surface question - are the error traces safe to share? we need to scrub pII before handing to vendor for SOC2 audit.
[01:58] Samir: absolutely, we'll provide redacted traces. we can mask tokens and user ids; Jenna will handle scrub.
[02:08] Carlos: what's the recommended retry strategy? we see our clients retry immediately which we think made it worse.
[02:15] Jenna: first: add exponential backoff with jitter (start 100ms, double, cap at 2s) and limit retries to 2. second: add client-side concurrency limit - we recommend max in-flight per-user of 8 for your access patterns.
[02:34] Carlos: ok makes sense. but if we reduce retries we'll drop more requests visible to users - tradeoff.
[02:40] Samir: tradeoff yes, but amplified retries can cause cascading failure. better to fail fast + graceful degrade or use cached response, and let us increase rate limit temporarily while we tune.
[02:52] Tom B.: can you do a temporary rate bump? our spike tests are scheduled tomorrow.
[02:56] Samir: yes we can provide a temporary increase for the poc window. i'll send details and limits.
[03:03] Jenna: other low-level: KV cache cold-miss was high. the model variant we used has a larger KV working set, and when long sequences hit the cache it caused memory pressure and slowed kernel swaps. we have a small patch for smarter prefetch and async eviction that we can test in your staging.
[03:22] Aisha: that patch - any risk to correctness or increased latency for normal requests?
[03:26] Jenna: it's opt-in, and in our internal tests it reduced tail latency by 18% on similar patterns. no correctness changes.
[03:35] Carlos: great. for the 5xx window do you see it as infra-level or model-level issue?
[03:40] Jenna: primarily infra-level - queuing and resource contention - though the model variant choice (long-context) increases resource footprint.
[03:48] Speaker 1: (mumble) also noticed some rate-limit 429s in the logs around the same time, possibly from a misconfigured retry policy.
[03:55] Samir: good catch. we will correlate API gateway 429s with client retry bursts.
[04:01] Marta: from compliance perspective, we need audit logs for any fallback to hosted vs private routing. our legal team asks for proof we didn't route PII to non-approved regions.
[04:12] Samir: understood. Redwood will include routing metadata in the audit bundle. we'll mark which region and which model instance served each request.
[04:20] Carlos: timeline - if we accept the patch and retry changes, how quickly can we verify?
[04:25] Jenna: patch testing in staging could be done in 48 hours; then we recommend a controlled load test for 2 hours to validate.
[04:31] Tom B: we'll run that test on monday if you can bump rate limits over the weekend.
[04:36] Samir: yes i'll authorize a temporary increase through 2026-05-10 for the POC account. details in email.
[04:43] Jenna: next up - observability. we suggested adding per-route percentile dashboards and token-level tracing for the POC. Carlos, do you want token-level traces going to your S3 or do we provide a signed bundle?
[04:55] Carlos: signed bundle is fine but we need retention to be 90 days and access controls.
[05:02] Samir: we can do 90-day retention for the POC audit logs; longer is an add-on. i'll note that.
[05:09] Aisha: also, can we get more granular rate-limiting rules - per-user and per-route? currently it's account-wide.
[05:16] Jenna: yes the console supports per-route quotas and token buckets. we can push config changes and test with your staging tokens.
[05:24] Carlos: ok good. anything on cost? some of these long-context runs cause GPU memory shifts and cost spikes.
[05:30] Samir: we recommended different model variants and quantization profile to reduce cost - we'll share cost delta spreadsheet. for POC we'll cover the temporary bump.
[05:40] Tom B: one operational question - do you support circuit-breaker upstream so our clients stop sending when host error rate crosses threshold?
[05:46] Jenna: yes we support circuit-breaker patterns via config. we can push an example config which trips at 5% 5xx over 5 minutes.
[05:55] Carlos: please do.
[05:58] Samir: quick recap before we go through open items. jenna will scrub and share traces, add patch for kv-cache to staging, samir will arrange rate-limit increase and send doc with limits and pricing, carlos/aisha will run load test and try the new retry/backoff pattern.
[06:12] Marta: security asks that we receive an answer on where audit logs are stored, encryption at rest, and SSO flow notes by next wednesday.
[06:20] Samir: noted - i'll include answers in the security bundle by 2026-05-06.
[06:26] Jenna: one more technical note - if you see 5xxs from a specific model shard, please capture the host id and hang time, that helps us root cause kernel-level OOM vs inference queueing.
[06:37] Tom B: will do.
[06:39] Speaker 2 (muffled): also a couple of the errors had odd ngrams in the prompt that caused early tokenization errors - might be client side.
[06:49] Aisha: worth flagging. we'll sanitize inputs preflight.
[06:53] Samir: perfect. ok let's go down the action items one more time - jenna, traces + scrub by 2026-05-06; samir, temp rate-limit and doc by 2026-05-05; carlos/aisha, run extended load test and try retry/backoff by 2026-05-08; schedule deep-dive on 2026-05-10. anything else?
[07:17] Carlos: no that's it. thanks.
[07:20] Samir: thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links and the security bundle.
[07:25] Jenna: thanks, bye.
[44:00] (call ended)
